question.text: An investor's PMS portfolio generates Rs. 8 lakh in interest income. The investor's marginal slab rate is 30%, and a 4% health and education cess applies on tax; surcharge is not applicable. The approximate total tax on this interest is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Interest income is taxed at slab rates (NISM-Series-XXI-A workbook pp. 160, 165). Tax before cess = Rs. 8,00,000 x 30% = Rs. 2,40,000. Adding 4% health and education cess = 2,40,000 x 1.04 = Rs. 2,49,600. The Trap: Rs. 2,40,000 is the tax before cess and is defensible if the stem is read to ask "tax before cess" (the audit flagged this ambiguity). Rs. 3,00,000 assumes a flat 37.5% which is not the slab. Rs. 1,60,000 applies the wrong slab. With cess specified, Rs. 2,49,600 is the uniquely correct figure. Note: The original stem said "30%+cess" without naming the cess rate or excluding surcharge, leaving Rs. 2,40,000 and Rs. 2,49,600 both defensible. The stem now explicitly fixes the cess at 4% (health and education cess) with no surcharge, anchoring the answer to Rs. 2,49,600 (NISM-Series-XXI-A pp. 160 and 165).
